story:
Ava loved the second-grade science classroom, especially when they studied dinosaurs. Today, Ms. Lily had set up a big, bumpy table for their group activity. The goal was to build a prehistoric ecosystem using fossil replicas. Ava was incredibly *curious* [emotion:QT/happy], because she wanted to build the biggest, most detailed T-Rex habitat. She gathered tiny, painted bones and miniature fern plants, arranging them in a perfect, careful line.

When her friend, Leo, walked over, he wanted to add a cluster of blue, crystalline geodes. Ava started to arrange her bones, but Leo reached across her work area, and *clink!* A tiny, essential bone rolled away and disappeared under the edge of the table. Ava felt a rush of *frustrated* emotion. She wanted to cry, but she remembered what Ms. Lily taught them about staying calm. She looked at the bone-shaped gap and whispered, "Oh no, where did it *go*?"

Leo knelt down, looking thoughtful. "I am so *sorry* that happened," he said. Ms. Lily gently knelt beside them. "It is okay to feel frustrated, Ava," Ms. Lily explained. "Remember that sometimes we need to *take turns* when we are building together, because sharing space helps everyone learn." Ava sighed, feeling a little *nervous*. She realized she needed help. She took a deep breath and spoke, "Ms. Lily, can you help me find it? I need to *share* my bones."

Ms. Lily smiled and pointed to the edge of the table. "Look, Ava. You see that tiny, dark corner? Leo, can you use your big flashlight? And Ava, remember to *listen* carefully for the smallest sounds." Leo carefully shone his flashlight, and *there* it was! The bone was caught in a tangle of woven blue moss. Ava let out a breath of *relieved* air. She felt so *proud* of herself for asking for help.

They worked together, carefully rescuing the bone. Because they cooperated, they managed to put the bone back in the perfect spot. Ms. Lily helped them build a little ramp so the T-Rex could walk over it. "You see, Ava?" Ms. Lily said. "When we work as a team, we can build much bigger and stronger things, so that we can learn more." Ava and Leo laughed and spent the rest of the afternoon decorating their amazing, collaborative dinosaur world.
